chunks: I said to Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: A man passes through, intending Yemen or another of the towns, and his route is through Mecca. Then he catches up with the people while they are going out for hajj, so he goes out with them to the sacred sites. Will that suffice for him as the Hajj of Islam?

key_terms.الْمَشَاهِدِ: the sacred sites or ritual stations of hajj
key_terms.حَجَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required in Islam
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the city through which his route passes

ai.seo_question: Does hajj count as the obligatory Hajj of Islam for someone who only joined the pilgrims while passing through Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a traveler who passes through Mecca without originally setting out specifically for hajj. If he joins the pilgrims and performs the hajj, it suffices for his obligatory Hajj of Islam.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "A man passes through on his way to Yemen or another city, and his route takes him through Mecca. He finds people preparing to go out for Hajj, so he joins them and performs the rites. Does this suffice as the Hajj of Islam for him?"
